area: Environment as Steering Pressure for Coding Agents: Test/Lint Feedback, Scope Enforcement, Definition of Done, SWE-bench Harnesses, and Memory/Skill-Acquisition Agents

mechanisms.name: Fail-to-Pass Test Oracle (SWE-bench Harness Pattern)
mechanisms.whatItIs: The SWE-bench evaluation harness defines completion not as the agent claiming it is done but as empirical proof: a designated set of tests that were failing before the patch must pass after it (FAIL_TO_PASS), and no previously-passing tests may break (PASS_TO_PASS). Each task ships a Docker image that pins the exact repo snapshot, dependency versions, and build toolchain, so test outcomes are fully reproducible. The agent's patch is applied as a git diff, the test suite runs, and only a clean flip of all FAIL_TO_PASS cases with no PASS_TO_PASS regressions constitutes a resolved task. Crucially, ~31% of benchmark instances have test suites weak enough to pass semantically wrong patches, exposing that the oracle quality is itself a design variable.
mechanisms.evidence: SWE-bench original paper (ICLR 2024, arXiv:2310.06770) and swebench.com describe the three-stage construction pipeline (scrape PRs → filter for issue-linked test changes → retain only fail-to-pass instances). GitHub issue #257 on SWE-bench/SWE-bench documents the PASS_TO_PASS / FAIL_TO_PASS distinction. The 31% weak-oracle figure comes from the arXiv:2506.10954 SWE-Factory paper.
mechanisms.applicability: pi-goal can adopt this pattern directly in its COMPLETION GATE: instead of relying solely on the agent's self-reported evidence, the gate should automatically run the project test suite (via exec) and require that every test that was failing when the goal was set must now pass, and no previously-passing test may be newly broken. The gate blocks goal_complete unless this binary condition is satisfied, making the environment the authoritative judge rather than the LLM.

mechanisms.name: LLMLOOP: Layered Iterative Environment Feedback Loops
mechanisms.whatItIs: LLMLOOP (ICSME 2025, arXiv:2603.23613) is a framework that wraps an LLM code-generation loop with five sequential automated feedback stages: (1) resolve compilation errors, (2) address static analysis / lint issues, (3) fix test case failures, (4) improve test quality via mutation analysis, and (5) check coverage thresholds. Each stage runs a tool, captures structured output (error messages, line numbers, mutation kill rates), and re-prompts the LLM with that output as the sole corrective context. The loop terminates only when all five stages pass simultaneously. It runs inside a Docker sandbox so generated code cannot affect the host.
mechanisms.evidence: arXiv:2603.23613 and its ICSME 2025 Tool Demonstration Track entry at conf.researchr.org describe all five loops and the Docker sandbox in detail. ResearchGate mirrors the full paper.
mechanisms.applicability: pi-goal's tool_call/tool_result hooks can implement an equivalent multi-stage loop without a separate framework. On every file-write tool result, a postToolUse hook fires the project's linter (e.g., eslint, ruff, mypy) and compiler/typecheck (e.g., tsc --noEmit), captures stdout/stderr, and injects failures as additionalContext back into the agent's context window so the agent sees them in the very next turn. A separate hook fires after the agent emits any signal that it considers a task done, runs the full test suite, and blocks goal_complete if any stage is red. This maps LLMLOOP's five stages onto pi's existing hook machinery.

mechanisms.name: PostToolUse Hook Context Injection (Claude/pi Agent SDK Pattern)
mechanisms.whatItIs: Agent SDKs that support hooks expose two injection points around every tool call: a preToolUse hook that can approve, block, or rewrite arguments before execution, and a postToolUse hook that fires after the tool succeeds and can inject text back into the model's context window via an additionalContext field. This allows the host environment to silently append structured feedback — lint results, test pass/fail counts, type errors, diff stats — without requiring the agent to explicitly ask for that information. The agent sees the feedback as part of its context before composing its next action, effectively turning every tool invocation into a mini reward signal.
mechanisms.evidence: Claude Code Agent SDK documentation at code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks and platform.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks describe updatedToolOutput and additionalContext as the two return fields for postToolUse. The Pixelmojo blog post 'Claude Code Hooks: 6 Production Patterns (2026)' and the Dotzlaw Consulting article 'Claude Code Hooks: The Deterministic Control Layer' describe the pattern of running a linter inside a postToolUse hook and injecting errors. A known limitation is documented in github/copilot-cli issue #2980: some implementations capture hook output but do not forward additionalContext to the context window, so the pi extension must confirm it correctly forwards this field.
mechanisms.applicability: pi-goal already intercepts tool_call and tool_result events. The immediate improvement is: on every tool_result for a file-write or shell-exec event, run lint and typecheck in the hook handler, and if there are failures, prepend them to the injected context with a structured header such as '[ENVIRONMENT FEEDBACK - must fix before proceeding]'. This is zero-latency corrective pressure applied before the agent's next token is generated, making the environment an always-on steering signal rather than a gating check only at completion.

mechanisms.name: SWE-RM: Execution-Free Reward Model as Continuous Judge
mechanisms.whatItIs: SWE-RM (arXiv:2512.21919, Dec 2025) is a mixture-of-experts reward model (30B total, 3B activated) trained to score software engineering agent trajectories without running any code. It discriminates between successful and failing agent trajectories by reading the sequence of tool calls, diffs, and reasoning steps, returning a continuous quality score rather than a binary pass/fail. When used at test-time as a candidate ranker, it raised Qwen3-Coder-Flash from 51.6% to 62.0% and Qwen3-Coder-Max from 67.0% to 74.6% on SWE-Bench Verified. Its value is highest when execution feedback is unavailable (no test suite, or test suite inadequate) and as a supplement to execution-based oracles to catch plausible-but-wrong patches.
mechanisms.evidence: arXiv:2512.21919 abstract and OpenReview PDF (openreview.net/pdf?id=H9wMe1G76j) report the architecture (MoE, 30B/3B), the SWE-Bench Verified accuracy numbers, and the test-time scaling (TTS) use case. EmergentMind topic pages for 'SWE-RM Verifier' and 'Execution-Free Feedback' summarize the mechanism.
mechanisms.applicability: pi-goal's COMPLETION GATE currently relies on the agent filling in structured evidence fields. Adding an LLM-as-judge layer at goal_complete time — either calling a hosted reward model or prompting a smaller judge model with the full task trace — gives a second opinion before accepting the gate. The judge receives the original goal spec, the task list, the diff produced, and the test results, and must score completeness and correctness above a threshold. This is directly implementable via pi's exec hook (call an API) or by spawning a judge subagent at agent_end.

mechanisms.name: Spec-Driven Out-of-Scope Enforcement
mechanisms.whatItIs: Spec-driven development (SDD), formalized as a 2025-2026 engineering practice by Thoughtworks and GitHub, treats a machine-readable specification as a live coordination document for both agents and CI. A well-formed spec defines six elements: desired outcomes (not feature names), explicit in-scope behaviors, an equally explicit out-of-scope list, hard constraints (stack, auth, performance), prior decisions already made, and verifiable acceptance criteria. The out-of-scope list is treated as a blocking constraint: any diff that touches files, modules, or behaviors named in the out-of-scope section is flagged. GitHub open-sourced a CLI called 'specify' in September 2025 with slash commands for Claude Code, Cursor, and Copilot that validate diffs against the spec. The key insight is that leaving out-of-scope behaviors undefined causes the agent to answer those open questions itself, in ways the user did not intend.
mechanisms.evidence: Augment Code's 'What Is Spec-Driven Development? A Complete Guide' and 'How AI Enhances Spec-Driven Development Workflows' explain the six-element spec structure and the out-of-scope enforcement mechanism. Thoughtworks' blog post 'Spec-driven development: unpacking one of 2025's key new AI-assisted engineering practices' contextualizes it as an industry response to AI throughput outpacing human review capacity. The BCMS 'Definitive 2026 Guide' and Medium/@Intellibytes post cover tooling.
mechanisms.applicability: pi-goal's goal-setting UX should require the user to provide not just a goal description and task list, but also an explicit out-of-scope section persisted in SQLite alongside the goal. The mission system prompt injected before every LLM call should include this out-of-scope list verbatim. A preToolUse hook should pattern-match file paths in write/edit tool calls against the out-of-scope list and block or warn when a match is detected. The COMPLETION GATE's required evidence fields should include a 'scope_adherence' field where the agent must enumerate every out-of-scope item and confirm it was not touched.

mechanisms.name: SWE-Search: MCTS Value Estimation for Exploration vs. Exploitation
mechanisms.whatItIs: SWE-Search (ICLR 2025, arXiv:2410.20285) augments a software agent with Monte Carlo Tree Search, replacing greedy linear execution with a tree of candidate patches. At each node, a Value Agent estimates a numeric utility score for the current state using LLM-based qualitative assessment (did the approach make progress toward resolution?) plus heuristics. A Discriminator Agent conducts a debate between candidate branches to select the best next action. Exploration vs. exploitation is balanced via an AlphaZero-style UCB formula applied to the value estimates. The result is a 23% relative improvement across five models on SWE-bench compared to greedy single-trajectory agents.
mechanisms.evidence: ICLR 2025 proceedings at proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/file/a1e6783e4d739196cad3336f12d402bf-Paper-Conference.pdf and arXiv:2410.20285v3 describe the MCTS architecture, the Value Agent/Discriminator Agent design, and the 23% improvement figure. EmergentMind paper page (emergentmind.com/papers/2410.20285) summarizes the result.
mechanisms.applicability: pi-goal can approximate the Value Agent without full MCTS by using its session-forking capability to spawn parallel subagent branches on complex tasks where the implementation strategy is unclear, then use an LLM judge to score each branch's intermediate state (does the diff look coherent? do partial tests pass? is scope maintained?) before committing to one path. The pi extension API supports fork/spawn sessions, making this a natural fit. Even without full MCTS, adding a value-estimation step at each major task checkpoint — implemented as a lightweight subagent call — provides richer steering signal than pure test pass/fail.

mechanisms.name: Trace2Skill: Parallel Trajectory Distillation into Reusable Skill Documents
mechanisms.whatItIs: Trace2Skill (arXiv:2603.25158, March 2026) addresses the scalability bottleneck of manually authoring skills for an agent by instead running the agent on a diverse pool of tasks, collecting the resulting execution traces, and dispatching a fleet of parallel sub-agents to analyze batches of those traces. Each sub-agent proposes targeted patches to a shared skill document: success-analyst sub-agents extract what worked and why, error-analyst sub-agents extract what failed and what should be avoided. The patches are then inductive-reasoned into a single, conflict-free skill directory. Trace2Skill consistently outperforms both human-written skills and sequential single-trajectory skill extraction on benchmarks.
mechanisms.evidence: arXiv:2603.25158 abstract and Hugging Face paper page describe the three-stage pipeline (trajectory generation → parallel patch proposal by success/error analysts → hierarchical consolidation). The alphaxiv.org resource page gives detailed methodology. EmergentMind 'Experience Compression Spectrum' (arXiv:2604.15877) frames skills as 50-500x compressed experience relative to raw traces.
mechanisms.applicability: pi-goal's agent_end hook is the natural place to trigger a background skill-distillation agent. After a session ends, the extension saves the full tool-call trace to SQLite (already done for tasks/evidence). A background process then runs a Trace2Skill-style analysis: it segments the trace into successful subtask completions and failed attempts, extracts reusable patterns (how a particular testing framework was debugged, how a migration was structured, which lint rules required specific workarounds), and writes them as named skill documents into the extension's resources_discover endpoint. Subsequent sessions discover and inject these skills as context, enabling cross-session learning without model fine-tuning.

mechanisms.name: MUSE-Autoskill: Skill Lifecycle with Unit-Test Gating
mechanisms.whatItIs: MUSE-Autoskill (arXiv:2605.27366, May 2025, ByteDance) defines a complete skill lifecycle within a running agent session: the agent identifies a need, calls a 'skill_create' tool to author a new procedural skill document, the framework immediately subjects the skill to its own unit tests, and only if those tests pass is the skill added to the skill bank for future reuse. A multi-level memory system — short-term (session), long-term (cross-session), and skill-level (per-skill execution history) — accumulates evidence about when each skill succeeds or fails. When a skill's accumulated evidence degrades (it starts failing more often), it is automatically scheduled for refinement. The framework is training-free and operates entirely through in-context tool calls.
mechanisms.evidence: arXiv:2605.27366 and the Pebblous blog post 'MUSE-Autoskill Self-Evolving AI Agents — The Skill Lifecycle Era' describe the skill_create tool, the unit-test gate on skill admission, the three memory levels, and the refinement trigger. The chatpaper.ai paper detail page confirms ByteDance authorship and the training-free claim.
mechanisms.applicability: pi-goal can implement a simplified version of the skill lifecycle: when the agent repeatedly uses the same pattern across multiple tasks in a session (detected by analyzing tool-call sequences in SQLite), the extension synthesizes a candidate skill document and stores it as a resource. The COMPLETION GATE can require the agent to nominate any reusable patterns from the session as part of its structured evidence (a 'skills_discovered' field), which forces the agent to reflect on transferable knowledge. These nominated skills feed the Trace2Skill background distillation pipeline described above.
